dialogues.speaker: Rika
dialogues.text: Oh, hey there! Looks like we're both in the competition. Are you here to pick up Yae Publishing House's latest novel, or do you want to jump right into the train simulation?

choices.text: Let's do the train simulation first.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: I'd only ever read about trains in light novels before. Hope you have fun too!

choices.text: Why are you selling novels? Aren't you an adventurer?

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: What, adventurers aren't allowed to sell things? I'm not the only one who does a little work on the side, you know...

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Adventuring gets expensive fast. Every commission, I burn through elemental potions and all kinds of other supplies. Then I get my reward, add everything up, and somehow I'm still out a few hundred thousand Mora.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: So what else can I do? Pick up some extra work, sell a few things here and there, and help pay the bills...

choices.text: Then why keep adventuring if it's such a money sink...?

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Absolutely not. A steady, by-the-book life? I'd be bored out of my skull before the week was over.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: What I want is to wake up somewhere new every day, meet people I've never met, see things I've never seen, and take on challenges I've never faced before.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: And for me, being an adventurer is the only way to live it.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Honestly, this competition has already been more than worth it. I've made friends from all over, and I've seen so many incredible things here in the land of ice and snow.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Too bad I'm hopeless at writing.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: I'll have to ask one of the editors to help me put together a letter for Souka, our resident deadline dodger. I'll tell her about everything I've seen lately, and maybe she can use some of it for her stories...

choices.text: If Mora's that tight, maybe you should get a regular job...

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Oh, they're fake! Just props. Same goes for the shrine maiden costume.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: A few years back, I took on an S-rank commission, which left me with way too much debt. After trying this and that, I somehow ended up working part-time at Yae Publishing House.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Then my luck turned around. The Irodori Festival was in full swing, so I got dressed up as a novel character and helped promote some collaboration drinks...

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: The promotion actually went really well. Aratani was happy with how I did, and I even got a nice bonus out of it.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: So ever since then, I've been working myself to the bone for Yae Publishing House. It's the steadiest job I've got.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Not that I'm stuck behind a counter or anything, though. I still spend most of my time traveling, camping, and adventuring all over the place.

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: And when I meet people on the road, I recommend light novels that fit the mood. That's where most of my sales come from!

response.speaker: Rika
response.text: Huh? Oh, alright... Well, if you ever get bored, come buy a book from me!
